hypotheses.title: With the same one-side tie-break on format pairs, waiting for the caller's trace ends with fewer failing checks than letting the helper owner act on the failing examples alone
With the same tie-break, waiting for the trace leaves fewer checks failing on fresh inputs than acting on the examples alone
The tie-break alone (no trace) ends with fewer failing checks than a manager agent
Waiting for the trace uses fewer tokens per case than a manager agent (harder tasks, two sizes)
